property_summary: For any caller and any msg.value, calling go() on the correct contract always leaves the contract owner richer by the contract's remaining balance (i.e., owner receives the contract's balance after go), whereas the mutant that transfers remaining balance to msg.sender instead can make the caller, not the owner, receive those funds for some inputs (fuzzer will find such inputs).

For every call to go(msg.value) the contract's owner address (owner()) ends up with increased balance by address(c).balance that was transferred out of the contract (i.e., owner receives the leftover contract balance); the mutant that sends leftover funds to msg.sender instead can cause the caller's balance to increase instead, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any msg.value, when C.go is invoked the contract's owner (owner()) ends up with strictly greater ether balance than the caller if and only if the external target call succeeds — the mutant that pays msg.sender instead can make the caller richer than the owner for some inputs (attacker target that accepts funds), so ownerBalance_after >= callerBalance_after fails for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any value sent to go(), after go() returns the contract's owner has the entire leftover balance that was in the contract (so address(c).balance == 0 and owner received the leftover funds); the mutant that transfers leftovers to msg.sender instead can leave the owner not having received those leftover funds for some inputs (an adversarial callee that accepts the forwarded value lets the leftover be nonzero or sent to caller), so the property is violated.

For every caller and any msg.value, after c.go(...) completes when the external target call succeeds, the reference always leaves address(c).balance == 0 and increases owner()'s balance by exactly the contract's pre-external-call leftover (so owner receives remaining balance), whereas the mutant that transfers remaining balance to msg.sender instead can leave owner()'s balance unchanged for some inputs; the test asserts owner balance increases when the callee accepts the forwarded funds.
